Maintenance review — 30 October 2026

Source: MAINTENANCE.md

Purpose and acceptance criteria

A configurable Mau Mau engine, reproducible simulations, and a local teaching app. This increment requires invalid counts to fail before coercion/allocation, existing legal play to remain compatible, a clean source package check, and a working installed first-use path. No rules or historical simulation data changed.

Findings and completed work

  • High: R/checks.R accepted infinity and values beyond integer range, producing missing values or unsafe allocation downstream. Counts now require finite bounded integers; regression tests include fractions, infinity, and overflow.
  • High: player strategy replication preceded the deck-capacity check. An impossible million-player deal could allocate a large list before failing. R/engine.R and R/simulate.R now check capacity first, using double arithmetic to avoid integer multiplication overflow, including zero-game simulations.
  • Packaging: linked-worktree .git metadata is excluded from source archives.

Validation

On macOS arm64, R 4.6.1: full source tests passed in 7.43 seconds. Source build with vignettes and complete R CMD check --no-manual passed, Status OK (build 62.13 s; check 39.01 s). The package installed by that check conserved all 32 cards at every step of 30 seeded games, all of which finished. A 25-game simulation repeated exactly and restored the caller’s RNG state.

The installed Shiny app, launched outside the checkout, passed Chromium checks for draw/pass, new game, win-rate table and plot, with no browser or Shiny errors. Evidence is retained in the workspace’s dated repository audit directory.

Use and remaining work

Follow README installation, then mm_play_game(seed = 1) or mm_run_app(). Existing tests cover stacking, skips, wilds, reshuffling and announcement rules. This review does not independently authenticate the physical card deck or rerun the historical 12,000-game README study. Its stated results are preserved.

Dependable-use repairs are complete locally. Optional future work is a cross-platform browser CI job and independently reproduced large simulation reports. Publication requires review/integration of this branch and a fresh remote CI run; no push, CRAN submission, or hosted app deployment occurred.
